errors.text: The proposed alloy and route do not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiTi powder-metallurgy system, high-energy ball milling, or spark-plasma sintering used in the target.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate the simultaneous production of sub-50 nm grains and an FCC+HCP solid-solution structure under the proposed 400–600 °C annealing conditions.

The assertion that C or N lowers stacking-fault energy and stabilizes HCP in a near-equiatomic FeMnCoCrNi alloy is composition-dependent and is not established by the cited evidence; interstitial carbon can instead stabilize FCC or suppress transformation in some systems.
High configurational entropy does not by itself guarantee suppression of carbides, nitrides, ordered phases, or other brittle precipitates.

The proposed falsification experiment confounds interstitial solid-solution strengthening with grain-size changes, phase transformation, and precipitation, so it cannot cleanly distinguish the claimed mechanism from simple solid-solution strengthening.
